say.text: Then Isa went to Qutb ad-Din Khusraw ibn Talil.
All the people now obey Salah ad-Din, except you and al-Yaruqi. Whatever else, there is a bond between you and him: you are both Kurds, and you will not let the high command pass to the Turks.

So Ibn al-Athir reports his words. It was the politics of a camp of emirs, who counted their followings by origin; it does not speak for every Kurd or every Turk. Nur ad-Din, whom they all served, was himself regarded as a Turk.
A bond of blood is a fine thing to be reminded of. It is better when it comes with a fief.
By magnificent promises, and the offer of a larger fief, he brought Qutb ad-Din to submit to Salah ad-Din.
You will have it in the vizier's own hand.
